items.title: Superblocks
items.designers: Ajuntament de Barcelona; Salvador Rueda / BCNecologia
items.placement: Placed at the Sant Antoni superblock, one of several in the programme. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: Grouping nine Eixample blocks and pushing through-traffic to the perimeter turns interior streets into plazas, play space and shade.

items.title: The High Line
items.designers: James Corner Field Operations; Diller Scofidio + Renfro; Piet Oudolf
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: A disused freight viaduct on Manhattan's West Side planted as a linear park, with Oudolf's self-seeding planting design.

links.label: Friends of the High Line — History

items.title: Vauban
items.designers: City of Freiburg; Forum Vauban; Baugruppen co-housing groups
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: A former barracks rebuilt as a car-reduced district of resident-led building groups, tram access and Passivhaus-standard homes.

items.title: Cheonggyecheon
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: An elevated expressway was torn down and the buried stream beneath it brought back as a sunken public promenade.

items.title: Metrocable
items.designers: Metro de Medellín; Municipality of Medellín (social urbanism)
items.placement: Placed at Santo Domingo Savio, one station on the network. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: Cable-car lines linking hillside informal neighbourhoods to the metro, paired with library-parks and public works at each station.

items.title: The Sea Ranch
items.designers: Lawrence Halprin; MLTW (Moore Lyndon Turnbull Whitaker); Joseph Esherick
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: A coastal community planned from wind, hedgerows and meadows, with timber buildings clustered to leave the land open.

items.title: Aranya Housing
items.placement: Placed at the city centre, approximate. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: Sites-and-services housing with plinths, service cores and a street hierarchy, built so families could extend their homes over time.

items.title: Quinta Monroy
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: "Half a good house": the state subsidy pays for the hard half, and families build the other half themselves inside the frame.

items.title: Byker Wall
items.scale: ≈ 620 homes in the Wall; ≈ 1,800 on the estate
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: A long, colourful perimeter block shelters a low-rise estate designed together with the residents, with an on-site architect's office.

items.title: Finger Plan
items.designers: Regional Planning Office (Peter Bredsdorff, Steen Eiler Rasmussen)
items.placement: Placed at the city centre, approximate. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: Growth along five rail "fingers" from the "palm" of the city, with green wedges kept open between them.

items.title: Curitiba BRT
items.placement: Placed at the city centre, approximate. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: Dedicated busways with tube stations and level boarding, set out together with land-use rules along structural axes.

items.title: Habitat 67
items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: Stacked precast boxes give each apartment its own garden on the roof of the unit below: density with the qualities of a house.

items.title: Rotiers – Renovation of 46 housing units
items.designers: MULTIPLE Architecture & Urbanism; architecture team: FP architecture; structural engineering: GEI

items.brief: Renovation of a 1960s social housing building that gives it a renewed identity while keeping the qualities of its wooded setting.

items.title: Novéo

items.designers: Taillandier Architectes Associés (lead architect: Marinell Van Wyk; TAA Bordeaux); architecture office: Lanoire & Courrian

items.title: Hotel MS Collection Arouca

items.scale: 6,698 m²; part of a monastic complex classified as a National Monument since 1910, converted into a five-star hotel

items.brief: Part of a monastery classified as a National Monument since 1910, rehabilitated as a five-star hotel.

items.title: Photography Studio as Local Infrastructure

items.placement: Placed at the city centre, approximate. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: A flood-damaged neighbourhood photo studio rebuilt as a small civic space with a café, observatory and shop.

items.title: Oxford Street pedestrianisation
items.site: Oxford Street, City of Westminster (first phase: Orchard Street to Great Portland Street)

items.placement: Placed at the site. Position from OpenStreetMap.
items.brief: Almost a kilometre of Oxford Street is now traffic-free, as a trial phase before the permanent scheme is built.
